info.title: CsMesh - Structural code intelligence for C# and .NET under a token budget.
info.description: Structural answer engine for C# codebases. Answers agent questions about call paths, interface implementations and change blast radius under a hard token budget.

commands.name: context
commands.description: Everything structural about one symbol, in a single call

options.name: --budget
options.description: Maximum output tokens (default: 800, exits code 2 on overflow)

options.name: --depth
options.description: Reverse traversal depth for impact and entrypoints (default: 3)

options.name: --json
options.description: Output as a structured JSON envelope

options.name: --repo
options.description: Repository root

options.name: --help
options.description:
Print help information
NOTES:
Replaces chaining trace + impl + blast-radius + entrypoints when the question is
"what is this thing and what touches it". Sections are ordered by usefulness, so an
exhausted budget drops the tail rather than the answer.

commands.name: cycles
commands.description: Circular dependencies between types or namespaces

options.name: --namespace
options.description: Collapse to namespace level instead of type level

options.name: --budget
options.description: Maximum output tokens (default: 800, exits code 2 on overflow)

options.name: --json
options.description: Output as a structured JSON envelope

options.name: --repo
options.description: Repository root

options.name: --help
options.description:
Print help information
NOTES:
Recursion inside one type is not reported; only loops between types, or between
namespaces, which are design problems rather than control flow.

commands.name: diff
commands.description: Symbols a git diff touched, and what they reach

options.name: --staged
options.description: Diff the index instead of the working tree

options.name: --depth
options.description: Reverse traversal depth from each changed symbol (default: 3)

options.name: --budget
options.description: Maximum output tokens (default: 800, exits code 2 on overflow)

options.name: --json
options.description: Output as a structured JSON envelope

options.name: --repo
options.description: Repository root

options.name: --help
options.description:
Print help information
NOTES:
blast-radius takes a symbol; this takes a change-set. Changed lines are attributed to
the innermost declaration that spans them, so an index built before the edit will
attribute wrongly -- re-index first. Requires git on PATH.

commands.name: path
commands.description: Shortest route from one symbol to another (alias: why)

options.name: --budget
options.description: Maximum output tokens (default: 400, exits code 2 on overflow)

options.name: --depth
options.description: Maximum hops to search (default: 12)

options.name: --json
options.description: Output as a structured JSON envelope

options.name: --repo
options.description: Repository root

options.name: --help
options.description:
Print help information
NOTES:
Answers "why is this class involved in this request". Mediator dispatch, container
bindings and interface calls each count as one hop, so the path crosses them like any
other edge. Exits 1 when no route exists within the depth limit.

options.description: Output as a structured JSON envelope

options.name: --repo
options.description: Repository root

options.name: --help
options.description:
Print help information
NOTES:
'doctor' reports that a graph is, say, 91% resolved. This says which 9%. A missing
edge and an absent one look identical in every other command; this is the only place
they can be told apart. The sample is capped at 400 sites per index.

options.name: --help
options.description:
Print help information
EXIT CODES:
0 ok   1 not-found   2 over-budget   3 ambiguous   4 no-index
64 usage-error   70 internal-error
CONFIDENCE:
A row marked [... ?0.70 short-name-match] came from a name match, not a compiler
symbol. Treat anything below 0.80 as a lead to verify, not a fact. 'csmesh doctor'
reports how many such edges the graph holds.
